events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by moderate to heavy rainfall is
possible, especially in terrain and poor drainage areas.

* WHERE...Portions of central, north central, and northwest Wyoming,
including the following areas, in central Wyoming, Owl Creek and
Bridger Mountains. In north central Wyoming, Bighorn Mountains
Southeast, Bighorn Mountains West, Northeast Johnson County and
Southeast Johnson County. In northwest Wyoming, Absaroka Mountains
and Cody Foothills.

* WHEN...From Friday afternoon through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A slow moving weather system is forecast to trek across Wyoming
Friday through Sunday and bring abundant moisture to the region,
especially northern Wyoming, and thunderstorms. Multiple rounds
of thunderstorms are expected and will be capable of producing
moderate to heavy rainfall across the Watch Area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, urbanized street
flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

rainfall over recent burn scars, which may lead to flash flooding
and debris flows.

humidities, this results in heat indices from 95 to 100 degrees
for much of eastern Kentucky during the afternoon. There is a low
chance for showers or storms to provide limited and localized
relief today.

Try to limit time outdoors today during the afternoon, when heat
illness is most likely to occur. If going outdoors, drink plenty
of fluids and take breaks out of the sun.
